video_caption: In a brightly lit mosque or prayer hall featuring a red carpet with striped patterns, a man wearing a green traditional tunic, a brown waistcoat, a white prayer cap, glasses, and a beard is speaking and gesturing with his hands. He is explaining the requirements for prayer to another man in a green sweatshirt and blue jeans, who is listening attentively and occasionally nodding. Text overlays appear sequentially, first stating "1. Our body must be clean" (0:00-0:07), followed by "2. Our dress must be clean" (0:09-0:21). During the discussion of the second point, a third man, dressed in a light blue long shirt and white pants with a beard, briefly walks into the scene from the background, shakes hands with the man in the green sweatshirt, and then exits the frame. The speaker continues his explanation, and the text overlay then changes to "3. Place of Salat must be clean" (0:22-end). The background of the hall includes white walls, high ceilings with recessed lighting, bookshelves on the left, and a doorway with a sign on the right.

In an indoor setting resembling a mosque, characterized by red prayer carpets with yellow stripes and bright overhead lighting, two men engage in a conversation about Islamic prayer. The man on the left, dressed in a green thobe, brown vest, and white skullcap, actively speaks and gestures with his hands, often smiling. He explains various aspects of prayer to the man on the right, who wears a green long-sleeved shirt and jeans, attentively listening and occasionally mimicking gestures. Text overlays appear throughout the segment to highlight key points: "Body, Clothes and Place Must be Clean!" (0:13), with the speaker gesturing to his attire and the surroundings; "4. Qiblah: You must stand towards Kaaba" (0:16), accompanied by an image of the Kaaba, as he explains the prayer direction; a list of prayer times "Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha" (0:38); and "5. Niyyah: Make intention in your heart for the prayer" (0:42). Finally, an illustration and text "TAKBEERAT Posture 1, Instructions: Bring hands, palms open, up to ears, and place thumbs behind earlobes, and say, اللهُ أَكْبَر (Allahu-o-Akbar, Allah is the Greatest)" (0:51) appear as the speaker demonstrates the initial prayer posture, which the listener then attempts to replicate.

In a brightly lit prayer hall, a man with a beard, wearing a white skullcap, green tunic, and brown waistcoat, stands on the left, instructing a younger man in a green sweatshirt and dark pants on the right. The hall features a red carpet with prayer lines and a blue patterned wall on the left, with other men visible in the background. The instructor gestures with his hands while explaining, then demonstrates the prayer posture of raising hands with thumbs near the ears, palms forward, saying "Allahu Akbar." The student attentively listens, initially with his hands clasped, then mimics the gesture, raising his hands in the same manner as the instructor. The scene cuts to a wider shot at 0:23, showing both men standing side-by-side, executing the prayer gesture, before returning to the original medium shot where the instructor continues explaining, reinforcing the importance of the initial prayer phrase.

In a brightly lit prayer hall with a red carpet and prayer lines, two men stand facing each other. The man on the left, wearing a white skullcap, glasses, a light green traditional shirt (kurta), and a reddish-brown vest, is speaking and gesturing with his hands. He appears to be teaching or explaining something to the man on the right, who wears a dark green long-sleeved shirt and dark pants and listens attentively, occasionally nodding or making small hand gestures. As the man on the left speaks, text overlays appear on the screen: at 0:05, "سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَ بِحَمْدِكَ، وَ تَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَ تَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَ لا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ (O Allah, how perfect You are and praise be to You. Blessed is Your name, and exalted is Your majesty. There is no god but You.)" along with "[Beginning of the first Rak'ah]"; at 0:22, "أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of all the worlds.)"; at 0:28, "Suratul Fatihah (the opening chapter)"; and from 0:32 to 0:45, "الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ، إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ، اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ، صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ (The Beneficent, the Merciful. Owner of the Day of Judgement. You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help. Guide us on the straight path, The path of those who You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray.)" The background features white walls, a second-story balcony with a glass railing, and a doorway, suggesting an interior religious space.

In a well-lit mosque or Islamic prayer hall with red striped carpets and white walls, two men are engaged in conversation. On the left, a man with a dark beard and glasses wears a white kufi, a light green long-sleeved tunic, and a dark brown vest, gesturing with his hands as he speaks. He appears to be explaining something about reciting Quranic verses, mentioning "Al-Fatiha first and then other Quran verse" and clarifying that "any verses of the Quran, any smallest surah, ayat is verse is long, then what" is acceptable. Facing him, a younger man with black hair, dressed in a green long-sleeved sweatshirt and dark pants, listens attentively with his hands clasped in front of him. In the background, there's a raised platform or balcony, a dark door on the right, and various shelves and decor, including a circular ornate piece on the wall and some blurry text.

The video opens in a prayer room with a red carpet, where a man in a white cap and green thobe with a brown vest explains a prayer posture to another man in a green sweatshirt and jeans. An on-screen graphic overlay displays "RUKU Posture 3" with a diagram illustrating the bowing position. The accompanying text gives instructions: "Bend down at waist, placing palms of hands with fingers spread over knees. Back is parallel to ground, such that if a glass of water were on the back, it would not spill. Eyes looking down, directly ahead." The man in the cap verbally guides, instructing the other man to say "Allahu Akbar" (Allah is the Greatest) as they both begin to bow into the Ruku posture, bending their torsos forward at the waist while keeping their backs straight and parallel to the floor, hands resting on their knees. The on-screen graphic also displays "سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي الْعَظِيمِ" (SUBHAN A RABBIYAL AZEEM, Glory to my Lord, the Greatest) with instructions to recite it three times. The man in the green sweatshirt repeats the Arabic phrase after the man in the cap, who is demonstrating the correct form.

The video segment opens in a mosque with two men on a red carpet, demonstrating the "SAJJDAH Posture 5" of Islamic prayer. The man on the left, wearing a white cap and green kurta, is in a prostration position, followed by a man in a green sweatshirt and jeans. An on-screen graphic provides instructions for Sajjdah and the Arabic recitation "سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى" (SUBHANA RAB-BIYAL A'ALA), meaning "Glory to my Lord, the most high." As the man in the white cap slowly rises to a kneeling position, saying "Allahu Akbar" (Allah is the greatest), the man in the green sweatshirt imitates him. The man in the white cap then explains that during prostration, the hand, nose, and forehead should touch the ground, demonstrating the nose first, which prompts a laugh from both. They repeat the prostration (Sajjdah) with the man in the green sweatshirt reciting the prayer, after which both rise to a standing position while saying "Allahu Akbar." On-screen text asks, "Was this Fajr?" which is clarified by the answer, "It was major thing (Basic prayer)." The segment concludes with both men kneeling and sitting on the red carpet. In the background, another man can be seen sitting and reading during most of the video.

In a spacious, brightly lit prayer hall with a red carpet marked by yellow lines, a bearded man wearing a white prayer cap, a green long shirt, and a brown vest sits in a kneeling posture, facing and instructing a younger man in a dark green shirt who is also kneeling. The instructor is speaking and occasionally gestures with his right hand, while the student listens attentively. At the 0:08 mark, a white rectangular overlay appears on the right side of the screen, displaying text with the title "QUOOD Posture 8" and subheadings "Recitation" and "Instructions." It presents Arabic scripture with transliteration and English translation, starting with "AT-TAHI-YATU LIL-LĀHI WAS-SALAWATU WAT-TAYYIBĀTU." (All prayers and worship through words, action and sanctity are for Allah only.), followed by other verses related to salutations and bearing witness to Allah and Prophet Muhammad. The instructions explain when to stand up or keep sitting after Tashahhud during different types of Salah (prayer). A line drawing depicting the "Quood" posture is also included in this overlay. At 0:25, the text in the overlay changes to show more Arabic recitation with transliteration and English translation, beginning with "AL-LĀHUM-MA BĀRIK 'ALĀ MUHAMMAD-IW" (O Allāh, bless Muhammad) and continuing with blessings upon Prophet Muhammad and his followers, akin to blessings bestowed upon Ibrahim and his followers. The kneeling posture remains consistent for both men throughout the segment.

The video segment takes place inside a mosque with a red carpet featuring yellow stripe patterns, white walls, and a visible balcony area above. Initially, two men are seated on the carpet. The man on the left, wearing a white cap and a green tunic over white pants, demonstrates an Islamic prayer ending by turning his head to the right and then to the left, saying, "Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullah" (peace and the mercy of Allah be on you), which appears as text on the screen. The man on the right, dressed in a green long-sleeved shirt and dark pants, watches and then practices the same gesture, echoing the phrase. A third man with a beard is visible in the background, seated to the far left, engrossed in reading a book. Subsequently, the man in the white cap explains the significance of the "Salam" gesture to the man in the green shirt, stating, "Salam means peace upon you. Because angels here and here. This angel for writing, for calculate your good jobs. And this is for bad, yeah," gesturing to his right and left shoulders to represent the angels, while the other man listens intently.

In a brightly lit indoor setting, likely a mosque or prayer room, with a red carpet covering the floor and a tiled wall on the left, two men are seated on the floor in the foreground. The man on the left wears a green traditional outfit and a white cap, has a beard, and gestures with his right hand as he speaks, maintaining a friendly expression. He is explaining something to the young man on the right, who is dressed in a green sweatshirt and dark jeans, listening intently and occasionally nodding. In the background, to the left, another man with a beard, wearing a white and grey hoodie, is seated on a white mat next to a small table, engrossed in reading a book. Behind the two men in the foreground, there's a wooden bookshelf filled with books and various items on the wall, including a white clock and green signs. The man in traditional attire finishes his explanation, and at 0:19, a text overlay appears on the screen, stating, "Do you have any questions?" The young man then expresses, "It's not easy," at 0:21, and begins to stand up, moving into the foreground, and at 0:24, another text overlay appears, "It's really not easy," as he finishes standing.
